guitar.guitaristsText: John Lennon / George Harrison / Paul McCartney
guitar.modelsText: Rickenbacker 325/360-12, Gretsch, Epiphone Casino, Gibson J-160E
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: well documented across multiple guitars and eras — Lennon's Rickenbacker 325/Casino, Harrison's Gretsch/Rickenbacker 360-12, McCartney mainly bass (Hofner) with some guitar use.
guitar.notes: Original entry reasonable as a summary across three members and many guitars; kept as-is.

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain tight rhythm playing.
Provide slight compression and sustain for a consistent rhythm attack.
Simulate the light grit and bite of a vintage British overdrive without heavy distortion.
Emulate the bright, punchy sound of a Vox AC30/British tweed amp.
Provide the classic British cabinet tone and necessary midrange punch.
Boost the upper-mids and high frequencies to achieve 'jangly bite' and cut through a mix.
Add a subtle 'jangle' effect and widen the sound without sounding modern or overly wet.
blocks.gap: The Chorus is used to enhance the jangling quality, though the source material was dry. This adds necessary width for playback.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the 'small room' feel and add natural depth without excessive wash.

improvements.summary: Refine IR to capture a drier, more immediate 'small room' sound and enhance the upper-mid bite required for 60s pop.

proposals.reason: Enhance dry, immediate 'small room' feel and boost upper-mids bite.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and punch in the high end.
